summary.text: 场 is the simplified form of 場, a compound in which 土 points to ground and 昜 supplies the sound. 場 is recorded for ritual ground and grain-working ground, as well as broader kinds of place.

formation.text: The traditional graph 場 is phonosemantic: 土 contributes the ground-related meaning, while 昜 provides a phonetic cue. 场 corresponds to 場, though its specific graphic path is unresolved.

components.text: In 場, 土 contributes the category of earth or ground.
In 場, 昜 is the phonetic component. Its own early graphic interpretation is debated, but that does not undermine its sound role here.

sound.text: The Zhengzhang Old Chinese reconstructions share the rhyme and syllable shape, though their initials differ. Middle Chinese records likewise share the 陽 rhyme and syllable shape but have different initials; these are scholarly reconstructions and rhyme-dictionary categories, not direct recordings.
sound.system: Old Chinese: Zhengzhang Shangfang; Middle Chinese: rhyme-dictionary categories and Baxter transcription

components.text: 场 is the simplified graph corresponding to 場. A proposed derivation from a cursive form has not been verified, so the precise graphic route remains unresolved.

history.text: The traditional graph 場 is analyzed as 土 plus 昜 serving as a sound component. A small-seal form is listed, but no oracle-bone or bronze form is established in the cited records.
場 is also recorded in the variant form 塲, a graphic variant distinct from the simplified 场.
场 is identified as the simplified counterpart of 場; the specific route, including the proposed cursive derivation, remains unresolved.

uncertainties.text: 場’s earliest surviving attestation date and any oracle-bone or bronze form remain undetermined; the listed small-seal image could not be inspected.
The exact graphic route from 場 to 场, including the proposed cursive derivation, remains unresolved.
The earliest graphic interpretation of 昜 is debated, separately from its supported phonetic role in 場.

senses.text: An early dictionary account glosses 場 as a way or ground for sacrificing to spirits; another account interprets it as level ground used for ancient sacrifice. The first surviving occurrence is not dated here.
The same dictionary account gives 田不耕, an uncultivated field, as an alternative gloss. Its relation in time to the ritual-ground sense is unresolved.

senses.gloss: ground for processing or drying grain
senses.text: A further gloss is ground for grain processing; cited texts use the character for a grain-drying or threshing floor. The chronology connecting this use to the other early glosses is unresolved.
Textual examples record 場 for a general place and other venues. Modern glosses include open space, field, and market, but the available examples do not establish their order or semantic links.
A figurative use meaning a domain is recorded, though its date and development from a physical place are not established.
Classifier use is recorded, but its date and development from another sense are not established.

developments.text: Both senses are recorded, but a direct historical development from ritual ground to grain-working ground is not established.
A broadening from a specific working ground to a general place is plausible, but the dates and connecting steps are not documented.
The figurative domain may extend the physical-place sense metaphorically, though the transition itself is not documented.
Classifier use is attested, but whether or how it developed from the place sense is unresolved.

limitations.text: The cited textual uses are not individually dated, so they do not provide a full semantic chronology or establish the first surviving occurrence.
The evidence supports a 土-plus-昜 phonosemantic construction; it does not support borrowing the entire graph 場 for an unrelated word.
